questions.text: The correct figure that shows, schematically, the wave pattern produced by superposition of two waves of frequencies 9 Hz and 11 Hz is:
options: Figure (1) showing wave pattern with alternating peaks and troughs at regular intervals
Figure (2) showing wave pattern with varying amplitude envelope
Figure (3) showing wave pattern with beats in middle section only
Figure (4) showing wave pattern with varying amplitude throughout
questions.sol_text:
When two waves of different frequencies f1 = 9 Hz and f2 = 11 Hz are superposed, they produce a beat pattern.

Beat frequency = |f2 - f1| = |11 - 9| = 2 beats/sec

This means the amplitude of the resultant wave varies periodically with a frequency of 2 Hz.

The period of beats = 1/(beat frequency) = 1/2 = 0.5 seconds

This means the amplitude reaches maximum (constructive interference) and minimum (destructive interference) alternately, with the pattern repeating every 0.5 seconds.

In a 2-second interval shown in the graphs, we should see 2 × 2 = 4 complete beat cycles.

Figure (1) shows the correct beat pattern where:
- The envelope of the wave varies periodically
- There are 4 complete beat cycles in the 2-second time span
- The alternating constructive and destructive interference is clearly visible
- This matches the expected beat frequency of 2 Hz

questions.text: A source of sound S is moving with a velocity of 50 m/s towards a stationary observer. The observer measures the frequency of the source as 1000 Hz. What will be the apparent frequency of the source when it is moving away from the observer after crossing him? (Take velocity of sound in air is 350 m/s)
questions.sol_text:
Observer is stationary, Source S is moving at 50 m/s towards observer initially.

The observer measures frequency as 1000 Hz when source approaches.

Using Doppler effect formula when source moves towards stationary observer:
f' = (V/(V - v_s)) × f_source

Where V = 350 m/s (velocity of sound), v_s = 50 m/s (velocity of source)

1000 = (350/(350 - 50)) × f_source

f_source = (1000 × 300)/350

Now when source moves away from observer after crossing:
f'' = (V/(V + v_s)) × f_source

f'' = (350/(350 + 50)) × (1000 × 300)/350

f'' = (300/350) × (350/400) × 1000

f'' = (300 × 350 × 1000)/(350 × 400)

f'' = (300/400) × 1000

f'' = 750 Hz

questions.text: A stationary source emits sound waves of frequency 500 Hz. Two observers moving along a line passing through the source detect sound to be of frequencies 480 Hz and 530 Hz. Their respective speeds are, in m/s⁻¹, (Given speed of sound = 300 m/s)
questions.sol_text:
Using Doppler effect formula for observer moving relative to stationary source:

For observer A (detecting 480 Hz - moving away from source):
n_A = n(v - v_A)/v = (500/300)(300 - v_A) = 480

500(300 - v_A)/300 = 480

500(300 - v_A) = 480 × 300

300 - v_A = (480 × 300)/500 = 288

v_A = 300 - 288 = 12 m/s

For observer B (detecting 530 Hz - moving towards source):
n_B = n(v + v_B)/v = (500/300)(300 + v_B) = 530

500(300 + v_B)/300 = 530

500(300 + v_B) = 530 × 300

300 + v_B = (530 × 300)/500 = 318

v_B = 318 - 300 = 18 m/s

Therefore, the speeds are 12 m/s and 18 m/s.

questions.text: A submarine (A) travelling at 18 km/hr is being chased along the line of its velocity by another submarine (B) travelling at 27 km/hr. B sends a sonar signal of 500 Hz to detect A and receives a reflected sound of frequency v. The value of v is close to: (Speed of sound in water = 1500 ms^(-1))
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Submarine A velocity: V_A = 18 km/hr = 5 m/s
- Submarine B velocity: V_B = 27 km/hr = 7.5 m/s
- Initial frequency: f_0 = 500 Hz
- Speed of sound in water: v = 1500 m/s

This is a two-step Doppler effect problem:

Step 1: Frequency received by A from B (B is source, A is observer)
f = [V - V_A]/[V - V_B] × f_0 = [1500 - 5]/[1500 - 7.5] × f_0

Step 2: Frequency received by B from A (A acts as source reflecting the sound, B is observer)
f' = [V + V_B]/[V + V_A] × f = [1500 + 7.5]/[1500 + 5] × [1500 - 5]/[1500 - 7.5] × f_0

f' = [(1500 + 7.5)/(1500 - 7.5)] × [(1500 - 5)/(1500 + 5)] × (500)

f' = [1507.5/1492.5] × [1495/1505] × (500)

f' = (1507.5 × 1495)/(1492.5 × 1505) × 500

f' = 502 Hz

⇒ t = x/v_plane = OB/v_sound
⇒ v_plane = v_sound · (x/OB)

From the geometry:
tan(30°) = x/h
⇒ x = h/sqrt(3)

OB = sqrt(h^2 + (h/sqrt(3))^2) = sqrt(h^2 + h^2/3) = sqrt(4h^2/3) = 2h/sqrt(3)

Therefore:
v_plane = v_sound · (x/OB)
= v · (h/sqrt(3))/(2h/sqrt(3))
= v · (h/sqrt(3)) · (sqrt(3)/(2h))
= v · 1/2
= v/2

questions.text: Two cars A and B are moving away from each other in opposite directions. Both the cars are moving with a speed of 20 ms^(-1) with respect to the ground. If an observer in car A detects a frequency 2000 Hz of the sound coming from car B, what is the natural frequency of the sound source in car B? (speed of sound in air = 340 ms^(-1))
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Car A (observer) moving with velocity v_A = 20 m/s (to the right)
- Car B (source) moving with velocity v_B = 20 m/s (to the left, away from A)
- Observed frequency n' = 2000 Hz
- Speed of sound v = 340 m/s
- Natural frequency n = ?

Using Doppler's formula for sound when both source and observer are moving:

n' = n[(v - v_0)/(v + v_s)]

where:
- v = speed of sound = 340 m/s
- v_0 = velocity of observer = 20 m/s (towards source, so positive)
- v_s = velocity of source = 20 m/s (away from observer, so positive)

Substituting the values:

2000 = n[(340 - 20)/(340 + 20)]

2000 = n[(320)/(360)]

2000 = n[8/9]

n = 2000 × (9/8)

n = 2000 × 1.125

n = 2250 Hz

questions.text: A uniform thin rope of length 12 m and mass 6 kg hangs vertically from a rigid support and a block of mass 2 kg is attached to its free end. A transverse short wavetrain of wavelength 6 cm is produced at the lower end of the rope. What is the wavelength of the wavetrain (in cm) when it reaches the top of the rope?
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Rope length L = 12 m, mass M = 6 kg
- Block mass m = 2 kg attached at free end
- Initial wavelength lambda_1 = 6 cm at lower end

The wave velocity in the rope depends on tension. As we move up the rope, tension increases, so wave velocity increases.

At the lower end (where block is attached):
T_1 = mg = 2g (tension due to block only)

At the top of the rope:
T_2 = (M + m)g = (6 + 2)g = 8g (tension due to rope and block)

Wave velocity is related to tension by:
V = sqrt(T/mu), where mu is mass per unit length

Since V is proportional to sqrt(T), and frequency remains constant:
V ∝ sqrt(T)

For a wave, V = f × lambda, so:
lambda ∝ V ∝ sqrt(T)

Therefore:
lambda_2/lambda_1 = sqrt(T_2/T_1)

lambda_2 = lambda_1 × sqrt(T_2/T_1)

lambda_2 = sqrt(8g/2g) × lambda_1

lambda_2 = sqrt(4) × lambda_1

lambda_2 = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

questions.text: The driver of a bus approaching a big wall notices that the frequency of his bus's horn changes from 420 Hz to 490 Hz when he hears it after it gets reflected from the wall. Find the speed of the bus if speed of the sound is 330 ms^(-1).
questions.sol_text:
The bus approaching the wall emits sound at frequency f_0 = 420 Hz. This sound reflects from the wall and is heard by the driver at frequency f_2 = 490 Hz.

Step 1: When the bus approaches the wall, the wall receives sound at frequency:
f_1 = (330/(330 - v_B)) × 420

Step 2: The wall acts as a stationary source reflecting this frequency. The driver (moving toward the wall) receives the reflected sound at frequency:
f_2 = ((330 + v_B)/330) × (330/(330 - v_B)) × 420

Step 3: Simplifying:
f_2 = ((330 + v_B)/(330 - v_B)) × 420

Step 4: Given that f_2 = 490 Hz:
490 = ((330 + v_B)/(330 - v_B)) × 420

Step 5: Solving for v_B:
490/420 = (330 + v_B)/(330 - v_B)
7/6 = (330 + v_B)/(330 - v_B)

Step 6: Cross-multiplying:
7(330 - v_B) = 6(330 + v_B)
2310 - 7v_B = 1980 + 6v_B
2310 - 1980 = 6v_B + 7v_B
330 = 13v_B

Step 7: Therefore:
v_B = 330/13 m/s
v_B = (330/13) × (18/5) ≈ 91 kmh^(-1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A sound source S is moving along a straight track with speed v and is emitting sound of frequency v₀ (see figure). An observer is standing at a finite distance, at the point O, from the track. The time variation of frequency heard by the observer is best represented by: (t₀ represents the instant when the distance between the source and observer is minimum)
options: Graph showing frequency dipping below v₀ at t₀ then returning to v₀
Graph showing frequency jumping down from above v₀ to below v₀ at t₀
Graph showing frequency starting above v₀, crossing v₀ at t₀, then dropping below v₀
Graph showing frequency peaking above v₀ at t₀ then dropping to v₀
questions.sol_text:
The Doppler effect for a moving source and stationary observer is given by:
f_observed = (v_sound / (v_sound - v cos θ)) × f₀

where θ is the angle between the source velocity and the line joining source to observer.

At t < t₀: The source is approaching the observer. The angle θ is such that cos θ is positive and decreases as the source gets closer. As θ decreases, cos θ increases, making the denominator smaller, so f_observed increases above f₀.

At t = t₀: The distance is minimum, meaning the source is moving perpendicular to the line joining source and observer. At this instant, θ = 90°, so cos θ = 0. Therefore:
f_observed = (v_sound / v_sound) × f₀ = f₀

At t > t₀: The source is moving away from the observer. The angle θ becomes obtuse, and cos θ becomes negative. The denominator increases, so f_observed decreases below f₀.

Therefore, the frequency starts above v₀, equals v₀ at t₀, and then decreases below v₀. This behavior is represented by graph (3).

questions.text: A transverse wave travels on a taut steel wire with a velocity of v when tension in it is 2.06 × 10^4 N. When the tension is changed to T, the velocity changed to v/2. The value of T is closed to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Three harmonic waves having equal frequency ν and same intensity I₀, have phase angles 0, π/4 and -π/4 respectively. When they are superimposed the intensity of the resultant wave is close to-
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Three harmonic waves with equal frequency ν and same intensity I₀
- Phase angles: 0, π/4, and -π/4

Since intensity I₀ ∝ A₀² for each wave, all three waves have the same amplitude A₀.

For phasor addition:
- First wave: amplitude A₀ at phase 0°
- Second wave: amplitude A₀ at phase π/4
- Third wave: amplitude A₀ at phase -π/4

Phasor diagram:
The second and third waves are at ±π/4 from the first wave.

Resultant amplitude calculation:
- Component along 0° direction: A₀ + A₀cos(π/4) + A₀cos(-π/4) = A₀ + A₀/√2 + A₀/√2 = A₀(1 + 2/√2) = A₀(1 + √2)
- Component perpendicular to 0°: 0 + A₀sin(π/4) + A₀sin(-π/4) = A₀/√2 - A₀/√2 = 0

Resultant Amplitude:
A = √[A₀²(1 + √2)²] = A₀(1 + √2)

A = A₀(1 + √2)

Resultant Intensity:
I_resultant ∝ A² = A₀²(1 + √2)²
I_resultant ∝ A₀²(1 + 2√2 + 2)
I_resultant ∝ A₀²(3 + 2√2)
I_resultant = I₀(3 + 2√2)
I_resultant = I₀(3 + 2 × 1.414)
I_resultant = I₀(3 + 2.828)
I_resultant ≈ 5.8I₀

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire of length L and mass per unit length 6.0 × 10^(-3) kg m^(-1) is put under tension of 540 N. Two consecutive frequencies that it resonates at are: 420 Hz and 490 Hz. Then L in meters is -
questions.sol_text:
V = sqrt(T/mu) = sqrt(540/(6×10^(-3))) = sqrt(90000) = 300 m/s

For a wire fixed at both ends, resonance occurs at frequencies:
f_n = n × V/(2L)

Two consecutive resonant frequencies are 420 Hz and 490 Hz.
The difference between consecutive frequencies is:
Δf = f_(n+1) - f_n = V/(2L) = 490 - 420 = 70 Hz

Therefore:
V/(2L) = 70

⟹ L = V/(2 × 70) = 300/(2 × 70) = 300/140 = 2.1 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A sound wave of frequency 245 Hz travels with the speed of 300 m·s^(-1) along the positive x-axis. Each point of the wave moves to and for through a total distance of 6 cm. What will be the mathematical expression of this traveling wave?
questions.sol_text: ω = 2πf = 2×3.14×245 = 1.5386×10^3 rad/s ≈ 1.5×10^3 rad/s. k = ω/v = (1.53×10^3)/300 = 5.1 m^(-1). A = 0.06/2 = 0.03 m (since total distance is 6 cm, amplitude is 3 cm). The wave equation is Y(x,t) = 0.03·sin(5x - (1.5×10^3)t).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: With what speed should a galaxy move outward with respect to earth so that the sodium-D line at wavelength 5890 A is observed at 5896 A?
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler's effect in light: v/c = Δλ/λ = (5896 - 5890)/5890 = 6/5890 = 3/2945. Therefore v = (3/2945) × 3 × 10^5 = 305.6 km/s ≈ 306 km/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Which of the following equations represents a traveling wave?
questions.sol_text: A traveling wave is represented by f(t ± x/v) where the argument contains both time t and position x in a specific linear combination. Option (B) y = Asin(15x - 2t) has the form f(15x - 2t), which represents a traveling wave moving in the positive x-direction with wave number k = 15 and angular frequency ω = 2. Option (A) has only time dependence in the argument. Option (C) has exponential decay. Option (D) has exponential decay in space. Therefore, the answer is (B).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A student is performing the experiment of resonance column. The diameter of the column tube is 6cm. The frequency of the tuning fork is 504 Hz. Speed of the sound at the given temperature is 336 m/s. The zero of the metre scale coincides with the top end of the resonance column tube. The reading of the water level in the column when the first resonance occurs is:
questions.sol_text: For first resonance, (l + 0.3d) = v/(4f). Given: d = 6 cm, f = 504 Hz, v = 336 m/s. Therefore: (l + 0.3 × 6) = (336 × 100)/(4 × 504). This gives: l + 1.8 = 33600/2016 = 16.67. Therefore: l = 16.67 - 1.8 = 14.87 cm ≈ 14.8 cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A tuning fork A of unknown frequency produces 5 beats/s with a fork of known frequency 340 Hz. When fork A is filed, the beat frequency decreases to 2 beats/s. What is the frequency of fork A?
questions.sol_text: When fork A produces 5 beats/s with 340 Hz fork, the frequency of A is either 340 + 5 = 345 Hz or 340 - 5 = 335 Hz. When fork A is filed (frequency increases), the beat frequency decreases to 2 beats/s. If initial frequency of A was 345 Hz, filing would increase it further, increasing beats. If initial frequency was 335 Hz, filing increases it toward 340 Hz, decreasing beats to 2 beats/s. So initial frequency of A is 335 Hz. After filing: |f_A - 340| = 2, which gives f_A = 342 Hz or 338 Hz. Since filing increases frequency from 335 Hz, the final frequency is 338 Hz (which is closer to the expected increase). Therefore, initial frequency of fork A is 335 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A closed-organ pipe of length L and an open pipe contain gases of densities ρ1 and ρ2 respectively. The compressibility of gases are equal in both the pipes. Both the pipes are vibrating in their first overtone with same frequency. The length of the open pipe is (x/3)sqrt(ρ1/ρ2) where x is ___. (Round off to the Nearest Integer)
questions.sol_text: For closed-organ pipe: 3λc/4 = L, fc = v/λc = 3v/(4L), where v/sqrt(ρ1) = constant. For open-organ pipe: λo = Lo, fo = v/Lo = v/L, where v/sqrt(ρ2) = constant. According to question, fc = fo, so (3v1)/(4L) = v2/Lo. Since compressibility is equal, v ∝ 1/sqrt(ρ). This gives Lo = (4L/3)sqrt(ρ1/ρ2). Comparing with given form (x/3)sqrt(ρ1/ρ2), we get x = 4.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A galaxy is moving away from the earth at a speed 286 km s^(-1). The shift in wavelength of a redline at 630 nm is x × 10^(-10) m. The value of x, to the nearest integer, is...............
questions.sol_text: Using the Doppler shift formula: Δλ = (v/c) × λ = (286/3000000) × 630 × 10^(-9) = 0.006 × 10^(-10) ≈ 6 × 10^(-10) m. Therefore, x = 6.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The frequency of a car horn encountered a change from 400 Hz to 500 Hz, when the car approaches a vertical wall. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s. Then the speed of car is ____ km/h.
questions.sol_text: Initially, the wall acts as an observer. Using Doppler's effect: f' = (c/(c - v_0)) * f_i. The wall receives frequency f' and acts as a source emitting sound of frequency f'. Using Doppler's effect again with the wall as source: f'' = ((c + v_0)/c) * f' = ((c + v_0)/c) * ((c)/(c - v_0)) * f_i = ((c + v_0)/(c - v_0)) * f_i. Given: f_i = 400 Hz, f'' = 500 Hz, c = 330 m/s. So: 500 = ((330 + v_0)/(330 - v_0)) * 400. Solving: 500(330 - v_0) = 400(330 + v_0). 165000 - 500*v_0 = 132000 + 400*v_0. 33000 = 900*v_0. v_0 = 33000/900 = 110/3 m/s = (110/3) * (18/5) = 132 km/h.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two cars are approaching each other at an equal speed of 7.2 km/hr. When they see each other, both blow horns of 676 Hz. The beat frequency heard by each driver will be..............Hz. [Velocity of sound in air is 340 m/s]
questions.sol_text: Convert speed: 7.2 km/hr = 7.2 × (5/18) = 2 m/s. Using Doppler effect formula for approaching sources: f'_B = f_A × [(v + v_B)/(v - v_A)] where v = 340 m/s, v_A = v_B = 2 m/s. f'_B = 676 × [(340 + 2)/(340 - 2)] = 676 × (342/338) = 676 × (171/169) = 684 Hz. Similarly, f'_A = 684 Hz. Beat frequency = |f'_B - f_B| = |684 - 676| = 8 Hz
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The percentage increase in the speed of transverse waves produced in a stretched string if the tension is increased by 4%, will be......%.
questions.sol_text: The speed of transverse waves in a stretched string is given by v = sqrt(T/μ), where T is tension and μ is linear mass density. When tension increases by 4%, new tension T' = 1.04T. New speed v' = sqrt(1.04T/μ). Percentage change = (v' - v)/v × 100 = (sqrt(1.04) - 1) × 100 ≈ (1.02 - 1) × 100 = 2%.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A source and a detector move away from each other in absence of wind with a speed of 20 m/s with respect to the ground. If the detector detects a frequency of 1800 Hz of the sound coming from the source, then the original frequency of source considering speed of sound in air 340 m/s will be ......Hz.
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula when both source and detector are moving away from each other: f' = ((v - v_d)/(v + v_s)) * f_0. Here v = 340 m/s, v_d = 20 m/s, v_s = 20 m/s, f' = 1800 Hz. Therefore: 1800 = ((340 - 20)/(340 + 20)) * f_0 = (320/360) * f_0. Solving: f_0 = 1800 * (360/320) = 1800 * (9/8) = 2025 Hz.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two travelling waves produces a standing wave represented by equation. y = 1.0 mmcos(1.57 cm^(-1))x sin(78.5 s^(-1))t. The node closest to the origin in the region x > 0 will be at x = ___ cm.
questions.sol_text: For a standing wave, nodes occur where cos(kx) = 0. This happens when kx = pi/2, 3pi/2, 5pi/2, ... For the first node closest to origin in x > 0 region: kx = pi/2, where k = 1.57 cm^(-1). Therefore, 1.57x = pi/2 = 3.14/2 = 1.57, which gives x = 1 cm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The mass per unit length of a uniform wire is 0.135 g/cm. A transverse wave of the form y = -0.21 sin(x + 30t) is produced in it, where x is in meter and t is in second. Then, the expected value of tension in the wire is x × 10^-2 N. Value of x is ________. (Round-off to the nearest integer)
questions.sol_text: From the wave equation y = -0.21 sin(x + 30t), comparing with standard form y = A sin(kx + ωt): k = 1 rad/m, ω = 30 rad/s. Wave velocity v = ω/k = 30/1 = 30 m/s. Mass per unit length μ = 0.135 g/cm = 0.135 × 10^-2 kg/m = 1.35 × 10^-3 kg/m. Using v = sqrt(T/μ), we get T = μv^2 = (1.35 × 10^-3) × (30)^2 = 1.35 × 10^-3 × 900 = 12.15 N = 1215 × 10^-2 N. Therefore, x = 1215.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A tuning fork is vibrating at 250 Hz. The length of the shortest closed organ pipe that will resonate with the tuning fork will be (Take speed of sound in air as 340 m/s^(-1))
questions.sol_text: For a closed organ pipe, the shortest length that resonates corresponds to the fundamental frequency where λ/4 = ℓ, therefore λ = 4ℓ. Using f = v/λ and λ = 4ℓ, we get f = v/(4ℓ), so ℓ = v/(4f). Substituting values: ℓ = 340/(4 × 250) = 340/1000 = 0.34 m = 34 cm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two cars X and Y are approaching each other with velocities 36 km/h and 72 km/h respectively. The frequency of a whistle sound as emitted by a passenger in car X, heard by the passenger in car Y is 1320 Hz. If the velocity of sound in air is 340 m/s, the actual frequency of the whistle sound produced is ......... Hz.
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula for approaching sources and observers: f' = f₀ × [(v + v_observer)/(v - v_source)]. Given: v_source = 36 km/h = 10 m/s, v_observer = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, f' = 1320 Hz, v = 340 m/s. Substituting: 1320 = f₀ × [(340 + 20)/(340 - 10)] = f₀ × [360/330]. Therefore, f₀ = 1320 × (330/360) = 1210 Hz.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire having a linear mass density 9.0 x 10^-3 kg/m is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of 900 N. The wire resonates at a frequency of 500 Hz. The next higher frequency at which the same wire resonates is 550 Hz. The length of the wire is _____ m.
questions.sol_text: Given: μ = 9 x 10^-3 kg/m, T = 900 N, f_n = 500 Hz, f'_n = 550 Hz. Wave velocity v = sqrt(T/μ) = sqrt(900/(9 x 10^-3)) = 1000 m/s. For a wire fixed at both ends, f_n = n*v/(2*l) and f'_(n+1) = (n+1)*v/(2*l). Setting up ratio: 500/550 = n/(n+1), which gives 10/11 = n/(n+1), so n = 10. From 500 = 10 * 1000/(2*l), we get l = 10 m.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The equations of two waves are given by: y1 = 5 sin 2π(x - vt) cm, y2 = 3 sin 2π(x - vt + 1.5) cm. These waves are simultaneously passing through a string. The amplitude of the resulting wave is:
questions.sol_text: y1 = 5 sin(2πx - 2πvt) cm. y2 = 3 sin(2πx - 2πvt + 3π) cm. Phase difference = 3π. A_net = sqrt(A1^2 + A2^2 + 2*A1*A2*cos(3π)) = sqrt(25 + 9 + 2*5*3*cos(3π)) = sqrt(34 + 30*(-1)) = sqrt(34 - 30) = sqrt(4) = 2 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A transverse wave is represented by y = 2sin(ωt - kx) cm. The value of wavelength (in cm) for which the wave velocity becomes equal to the maximum particle velocity, will be-
questions.sol_text: Given: y = 2sin(ωt - kx) cm, so A = 2 cm. Wave velocity v = ω/k = Aω. Maximum particle velocity = Aω. For wave velocity = maximum particle velocity: ω/k = Aω, so k = 1/A = 1/2 cm^(-1). Since k = 2π/λ, we have 2π/λ = 1/2, so λ = 4π cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For a specific wavelength 670 nm of light from a galaxy moving with velocity v, the observed wavelength is 670.7 nm. The value of v is
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler shift formula for light: λ_obs = λ_source × sqrt((1 + v/c)/(1 - v/c)). For v << c, this simplifies to: λ_obs/λ_source ≈ 1 + v/c. Therefore: 670.7/670 = 1 + v/c. This gives: 0.7/670 = v/c, so v = (0.7/670) × 3 × 10^8 = 3.13 × 10^5 ms^(-1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If a wave gets refracted into a denser medium, then which of the following is true?
options: Wavelength increases, speed decreases and frequency remains constant
Wavelength and speed decreases but frequency remains constant
questions.sol_text: Frequency is independent of medium. For denser medium, wavelength and speed both would decrease. When a wave enters a denser medium, its speed decreases due to increased optical density. Since frequency remains constant (it depends on the source, not the medium), and v = f × λ, the wavelength must also decrease proportionally.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An observer moves towards a stationary source of sound with a velocity equal to one-fifth of the velocity of sound. The percentage change in the frequency will be:
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula: f' = f0[(V + V0)/(V - Vs)] where V is velocity of sound, V0 is observer velocity, Vs is source velocity. Since source is stationary, Vs = 0 and V0 = V/5. Therefore: f' = f0[(V + V/5)/V] = f0[6V/5V] = 6f0/5. Percentage change = (f' - f0)/f0 × 100 = (6f0/5 - f0)/f0 × 100 = (f0/5)/f0 × 100 = 20%

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In the wave equation y = 0.5sin(2π/λ(400t - x))m, the velocity of the wave will be:
questions.sol_text: The wave equation is in the form y = A sin(2π/λ(vt - x)) where v is the wave velocity. Comparing y = 0.5sin(2π/λ(400t - x)) with the standard form, the coefficient of t is 400. Using v_wave = (coefficient of t)/(coefficient of x) = 400/1 = 400 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The velocity of sound in a gas, in which two wavelengths 4.08 m and 4.16 m produce 40 beats in 12 s, will be:
questions.sol_text: Beat frequency = 40 beats in 12 s = 40/12 Hz. For two wavelengths λ1 = 4.08 m and λ2 = 4.16 m with same velocity v: frequency difference f1 - f2 = v/λ1 - v/λ2 = 40/12. Therefore v(1/4.08 - 1/4.16) = 40/12. v × (4.16 - 4.08)/(4.08 × 4.16) = 40/12. v × 0.08/16.9728 = 40/12. v = (40/12) × (40.8 × 4.16)/0.08 = 707.2 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A longitudinal wave is represented by x = 10 sin(2*pi*(n*t - x/lambda)) cm. The maximum particle velocity will be four times the wave velocity if the determined value of wavelength is equal to -
questions.sol_text: Particle velocity = dx/dt. Maximum particle velocity = (2*pi)(10) = 20*pi. Wave velocity = (n*lambda)(4). Given: Maximum particle velocity = 4 × wave velocity. Therefore: (2*pi)(10) = (n*lambda)(4). Solving: lambda = 5*pi

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An observer is riding on a bicycle and moving towards a hill at 18 km/h. He hears a sound from a source at some distance behind him directly as well as after its reflection from the hill. If the original frequency of the sound as emitted by source is 640 Hz and velocity of the sound in air is 320 m/s, the beat frequency between the two sounds heard by observer will be ___ Hz.
questions.sol_text: Convert velocity: 18 km/h = 5 m/s. f3 = f0 = 640 Hz (no relative motion between source and hill). f2 = f0[(320 + 5)/320] = 640(325/320) = 650 Hz (observer moving towards reflected sound source). f1 = f0[320/(320 + 5)] = 640(320/325) = 630 Hz (observer moving away from direct sound source). Beat frequency = f2 - f1 = 650 - 630 = 20 Hz.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The first overtone frequency of an open organ pipe is equal to the fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe. If the length of the closed organ pipe is 20 cm. The length of the open organ pipe is ___ cm.
questions.sol_text: For closed organ pipe, fundamental frequency: f_c = V/(4*L_c). For open organ pipe, first overtone (second harmonic): f_o = 2*V/(2*L_o) = V/L_o. Given f_o = f_c, so V/L_o = V/(4*L_c), which gives L_o = 4*L_c = 4 × 20 = 80 cm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When a car is approaching the observer, the frequency of horn is 100 Hz. After passing the observer, it is 50 Hz. If the observer moves with the car, the frequency will be x/3 Hz where x = ____.
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula: When car approaches, f1 = v0 * v/(v - vc) = 100 Hz. When car recedes, f2 = v0 * v/(v + vc) = 50 Hz. Dividing: f1/f2 = (v + vc)/(v - vc) = 2. This gives: 2v - 2vc = v + vc, so vc = v/3. From first equation: 100 = v0 * (v × 3)/(2v), so v0 = 200/3. When observer moves with car, frequency = v0 = 200/3 Hz = (200)/3 Hz, therefore x = 200.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A set of 20 tuning forks is arranged in a series of increasing frequencies. If each fork gives 4 beats with respect to the preceding fork and the frequency of the last fork is twice the frequency of the first, then the frequency of last fork is ______Hz.
questions.sol_text: Given: 20 tuning forks in increasing frequency. Each fork gives 4 beats with respect to preceding fork, so the frequency difference between consecutive forks is 4 Hz. Last fork frequency is twice the first fork frequency. Let v1 = frequency of first fork. Then v20 = 2*v1. Also, v20 = v1 + 4*19 = v1 + 76. Therefore: 2*v1 = v1 + 76, which gives v1 = 76 Hz. So v20 = 2*76 = 152 Hz.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire of length 30 cm, stretched between rigid supports, has it's n^th and (n+1)^th harmonics at 400 Hz and 450 Hz, respectively. If tension in the string is 2700 N, it's linear mass density is _____ kg/m.
questions.sol_text: For a wire fixed at both ends, frequency of n^th harmonic is f_n = n*v/(2*L), where v is wave velocity. Given: f_n = 400 Hz and f_(n+1) = 450 Hz. The difference: f_(n+1) - f_n = v/(2*L) = 450 - 400 = 50 Hz. Therefore v/(2*L) = 50, so v = 50*2*0.3 = 30 m/s. Since v = sqrt(T/μ), we have 30 = sqrt(2700/μ), so 900 = 2700/μ, thus μ = 2700/900 = 3 kg/m.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The frequency of echo will be _______ Hz if the train blowing a whistle of frequency 320 Hz is moving with a velocity of 36 km/h towards a hill from which an echo is heard by the train driver. Velocity of sound in air is 330 m/s.
questions.sol_text: Convert velocity: v_s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/sec. The train moves towards the hill, so using Doppler effect formula: f = ((v + v_s)/(v - v_s)) × f_0 = ((330 + 10)/(330 - 10)) × 320 = (340/320) × 320 = 340 Hz
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A tuning fork of frequency 340 Hz resonates in the fundamental mode with an air column of length 125 cm in a cylindrical tube closed at one end. When water is slowly poured in it, the minimum height of water required for observing resonance once again is ____ cm. (Velocity of sound in air is 340 m/s)
questions.sol_text: Given: f = 340 Hz, initial air column length L = 125 cm, v = 340 m/s. For fundamental mode in closed pipe: f = v/(4L), so 340 = 340/(4×125), which gives n = 1 (fundamental). Wavelength λ = v/f = 340/340 = 1 m = 100 cm. For resonance in closed pipe, the air column length must be L = (2n-1)λ/4 where n = 1, 2, 3... First resonance: L₁ = λ/4 = 25 cm. Second resonance: L₂ = 3λ/4 = 75 cm. Initial length is 125 cm. Next resonance occurs at 75 cm. Minimum height of water required = 125 - 75 = 50 cm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of 20.0 cm for a tuning fork of frequency 400 Hz is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is 336 ms^(-1). The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____ cm
questions.sol_text: For resonance in a tube closed at one end: frequency = v / [4(L + e)] where L is length and e is end correction. First resonance: 400 = 336 / [4(L1 + e)], so L1 + e = 336/(4*400) = 0.21 m = 21 cm. Third resonance occurs at: 400 = 5v / [4(L2 + e)], so L2 + e = 5*336 / (4*400) = 1.05 m = 105 cm. Therefore e = 1 cm and L2 = 104 cm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two travelling waves of equal amplitudes and equal frequencies move in opposite directions along a string. They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by y = (10 cos πx sin(2πt/T)) cm. The amplitude of the particle at x = 4/3 cm will be _____ cm.
questions.sol_text: The amplitude of the stationary wave is given by A = |10 cos(πx)|. At x = 4/3 cm: A = |10 cos(π × 4/3)| = |10 cos(4π/3)| = |10 × (-1/2)| = |-5| = 5 cm
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A steel wire with mass per unit length 7.0 × 10^(-3) kg m^(-1) is under tension of 70 N. The speed of transverse waves in the wire will be
questions.sol_text:
Speed of transverse wave = sqrt(T/M)

= sqrt(70/(7 × 10^(-3)))

= sqrt(10000)

= 100 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The ratio of speed of sound in hydrogen gas to the speed of sound in oxygen gas at the same temperature is:
questions.sol_text: Speed of sound in a gas is given by v = sqrt(gamma*R*T/M), where M is molar mass. At same temperature, v is proportional to 1/sqrt(M). Therefore, v_H2/v_O2 = sqrt(M_O2/M_H2) = sqrt(32/2) = sqrt(16) = 4:1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The engine of a train moving with speed 10 ms^(-1) towards a platform sounds a whistle at frequency 400 Hz. The frequency heard by a passenger inside the train is: (neglect air speed. Speed of sound in air = 330 ms^(-1))
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula: f' = f₀[(v - v₀)/(v - vₛ)] where v = speed of sound = 330 ms^(-1), v₀ = speed of observer (passenger in train) = 10 ms^(-1), vₛ = speed of source (engine/whistle) = 10 ms^(-1). Therefore f' = 400[(330 - 10)/(330 - 10)] = 400[320/320] = 400 Hz. Since both source and observer move together at same speed, there is no relative motion, hence frequency remains 400 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A car P travelling at 20 ms^(-1) sounds its horn at a frequency of 400 Hz. Another car Q is travelling behind the first car in the same direction with a velocity 40 ms^(-1). The frequency heard by the passenger of the car Q is approximately [Take, velocity of sound = 360 ms^(-1)]
questions.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula for observer (Q) moving towards source (P): f = f0 * (C + v_observer)/(C - v_source) where C = 360 ms^(-1), v_observer = 40 ms^(-1), v_source = 20 ms^(-1), f0 = 400 Hz. Therefore f = 400 * (360 + 40)/(360 - 20) = 400 * (400/340) = 400 * (20/17) ≈ 471 Hz

questions.text: A travelling wave is described by the equation y(x, t) = [0.05 sin(8x - 4t)] m. The velocity of the wave is: [all the quantities are in SI unit]

Given: y(x, t) = [0.05 sin(8x - 4t)] m

For a wave equation of the form y(x, t) = A sin(kx - ωt), the velocity of the wave is given by:

Speed of wave = |Coefficient of t| / |Coefficient of x|

From the given equation:
Coefficient of t = -4
Coefficient of x = 8

Speed of wave = |-4| / |8| = 4/8 = 0.5 ms^(-1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A person observes two moving trains, 'A' reaching the station and 'B' leaving the station with equal speed of 30 m/s. If both trains emit sounds with frequency 300 Hz, (Speed of sound: 330 m/s) approximate difference of frequencies heard by the person will be:
questions.sol_text:
By Doppler effect : f' = f0[(v - v0)/(v - vs)]

For train A (approaching the station):
f_A' = 300[(330)/(330 - 30)] Hz
= 300[(330)/(300)] Hz
= 330 Hz

For train B (leaving the station):
f_B' = 300[(330)/(330 + 30)] Hz
= 300[(330)/(360)] Hz
= (5/6) × 330 Hz = 275 Hz

Difference of frequencies heard by the person:
f_A' - f_B' = 330 - 275 = 55 Hz

questions.text: For a solid rod, the Young's modulus of elasticity is 3.2 × 10^11 Nm^(-2) and density is 8 × 10^3 kg m^(-3). The velocity of longitudinal wave in the rod will be
questions.sol_text:
The velocity of longitudinal wave in a solid rod is given by:
v = sqrt(Y/ρ)

Where Y is Young's modulus and ρ is density.

Given:
Y = 3.2 × 10^11 Nm^(-2)
ρ = 8 × 10^3 kg m^(-3)

Substituting:
v = sqrt(3.2 × 10^11 / (8 × 10^3))
= sqrt((3.2/8) × 10^(11-3))
= sqrt(0.4 × 10^8)
= sqrt(4 × 10^7)
= 2 × 10^3 × sqrt(10)
= 6.32 × 10^3 m/s

questions.text: A person driving car at a constant speed of 15 m/s is approaching a vertical wall. The person notices a change of 40 Hz in the frequency of his car's horn upon reflection from the wall. The frequency of horn is ___ Hz. (Given: Speed of sound: 30 m/s)
questions.sol_text: The observer hears two frequencies: (1) Direct sound from horn as car approaches wall with Doppler shift, (2) Reflected sound from wall (wall acts as observer receiving frequency, then reflecting). For reflected sound, the wall receives frequency f' = f(v + v_s)/(v - v_observer) = f(330 + 15)/(330 - 15) = f(345/315). This reflected sound appears to come from wall approaching the observer: f_app = f'(v + v_observer)/v = f(345/315)(330 + 15)/330 = f(345/315)(345/330). The frequency difference is: f_app - f = f[(345/315)(345/330) - 1] = 40. Simplifying: f[(345 × 345 - 315 × 330)/(315 × 330)] = 40. This gives f = 40 × 315 × 330 / (345^2 - 315 × 330) = 40 × 315/30 = 420 Hz.

questions.text: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is equal to the first overtone frequency of an open organ pipe. If length of the open pipe is 60 cm, the length of the closed pipe will be:
questions.sol_text: For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency f_c = v/(4*l_c). For an open pipe, first overtone frequency f_o = 2*(v/(2*l_o)). Given: f_c = f_o and l_o = 60 cm. Therefore: v/(4*l_c) = 2*(v/(2*60)). Simplifying: 1/(4*l_c) = 2/(120). Thus: 1/(4*l_c) = 1/60, which gives l_c = 15 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length 1 m stretched with a tension of 6 N. When the tension in the wire is changed to 54 N, the same tuning fork produces 12 beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is _______ Hz.
questions.sol_text: Let f0 = tuning fork frequency. The frequency of sonometer wire is f = (1/2l)sqrt(T/μ). When T = 6 N: f0 = (1/2l)sqrt(6/μ). When T = 54 N: (1/2l)sqrt(54/μ) - (1/2l)sqrt(6/μ) = 12 (beat frequency). Therefore: (1/2l)sqrt(6/μ)[sqrt(9) - 1] = 12, which gives (1/2l)sqrt(6/μ) × 2 = 12. Thus (1/2l)sqrt(6/μ) = 6 = f0.

questions.text: A sonometer wire of resonating length 90 cm has a fundamental frequency of 400 Hz when kept under some tension. The resonating length of the wire with fundamental frequency of 600 Hz under same tension ______ cm.
questions.sol_text: For a sonometer wire, the fundamental frequency is given by f0 = v/(2L), where v is the wave velocity and L is the resonating length. Since tension is kept constant, the wave velocity v remains constant. For initial condition: f1 = 400 Hz, L1 = 90 cm. For final condition: f2 = 600 Hz, L2 = ? Since v = 2Lf0 is constant: 2L1*f1 = 2L2*f2, therefore L1*f1 = L2*f2. Solving: 90 × 400 = L2 × 600, L2 = (90 × 400)/600 = 36000/600 = 60 cm.

questions.text: A closed and an open organ pipe have same lengths. If the ratio of frequencies of their seventh overtones is (a-1)/a, then the value of a is ________.

The ratio f_c/f_o = (15v/4l)/(8v/2l) = (15/4) × (2/8) = 15/16. Given that this ratio equals (a-1)/a, we have 15/16 = (a-1)/a. Cross-multiplying: 15a = 16(a-1) = 16a - 16, so a = 16.

questions.text: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave x = a cos(1.5t) cos(50.5t) where t is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat (close to nearest integer)
questions.sol_text: Given: x = a cos(1.5t) cos(50.5t). Using product-to-sum formula: x = (a/2)cos(50.5t + 1.5t) + (a/2)cos(50.5t - 1.5t) = (a/2)cos(52t) + (a/2)cos(49t). Therefore f1 = 52/(2π) and f2 = 49/(2π). Beat frequency: Δf = |f1 - f2| = 3/(2π). Beat period: ΔT = 1/Δf = 2π/3 ≈ 2.09 ≈ 2 s. Note: The answer key shows [4] but calculation gives approximately 2 s.

questions.text: The amplitude and phase of a wave that is formed by the superposition of two harmonic travelling waves, y₁(x,t) = 4sin(kx - ωt) and y₂(x,t) = 2sin(kx - ωt + 2π/3), are: (Take the angular frequency of initial waves same as ω)

For phase: tanα = (A₂sinφ)/(A₁ + A₂cosφ) = (2sin(2π/3))/(4 + 2cos(2π/3)) = (2·sqrt(3)/2)/(4 - 1) = sqrt(3)/3 = 1/sqrt(3), so α = π/6.

questions.text: Two strings with circular cross section and made of same material are stretched to have same amount of tension. A transverse wave is then made to pass through both the strings. The velocity of the wave in the first string having the radius of cross section R is v1 and that in the other string having radius of cross section R/2 is v2. Then v2/v1 =

questions.text: Displacement of a wave is expressed as x(t) = 5 cos(628t + pi/2) m. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is 300 m/s is: (π = 3.14)

questions.text: A sinusoidal wave of wavelength 7.5cm travels a distance of 1.2cm along the x-direction in 0.3sec. The crest P is at x = 0 at t = 0 sec and maximum displacement of the wave is 2cm. Which equation correctly represents this wave?
questions.sol_text: Given: wavelength λ = 7.5cm, distance = 1.2cm, time = 0.3s, amplitude = 2cm, crest at x=0 at t=0. Wave number k = 2π/λ = 2π/7.5 ≈ 0.83 rad/cm. Wave speed v = distance/time = 1.2/0.3 = 4 cm/s. Angular frequency ω = kv = 0.83 × 4 ≈ 3.35 rad/s. Since crest is at x=0 at t=0, use cosine function with negative x-coefficient and negative t-coefficient: y = 2cos(0.83x - 3.35t) cm.

questions.text: In the resonance experiment, two air columns (closed at one end) of 100 cm and 120 cm long, give 15 beats per second when each one is sounding in the respective fundamental modes. The velocity of sound in the air column is:
questions.sol_text: For a pipe closed at one end, fundamental frequency f = v/(4L). For the 100 cm column: f1 = v/4(1) = v/4. For the 120 cm column: f2 = v/4(1.2) = v/4.8. Beat frequency = |f1 - f2| = 15 Hz. So |v/4 - v/4.8| = 15. Solving: v(1/4 - 1/4.8) = 15, v(4.8 - 4)/(4 × 4.8) = 15, v(0.8)/(19.2) = 15, v = 15 × 19.2/0.8 = 360 m/s.

questions.text: Consider the sound wave travelling in ideal gases of He, CH4 and CO2. All the gases have the same ratio P/ρ, where P is the pressure and ρ is the density. The ratio of the speed of sound through the gases V_He : V_CH4 : V_CO2 is given by
questions.sol_text: Speed of sound in a gas is v = sqrt(γP/ρ) where γ is the heat capacity ratio. Since P/ρ is the same for all gases, v ∝ sqrt(γ). For He (monoatomic): γ = 5/3. For CH4 (polyatomic): γ = 4/3. For CO2 (linear polyatomic): γ = 7/5. Therefore V_He : V_CH4 : V_CO2 = sqrt(5/3) : sqrt(4/3) : sqrt(7/5)

questions.text: In an experiment with a closed organ pipe, it is filled with water by (1/5)th of its volume. The frequency of the fundamental note will change by
questions.sol_text: For a closed organ pipe, the fundamental frequency is f = v/(4L) where v is speed of sound and L is length of air column. When water fills 1/5 of volume, the effective length becomes L' = L - L/5 = 4L/5. New frequency f' = v/(4 × 4L/5) = v/(16L/5) = 5v/(16L). Change in frequency: (f' - f)/f = (5v/16L - v/4L)/(v/4L) = (5v/16L - 4v/16L)/(v/4L) = (v/16L)/(v/4L) = (1/16) × (4/1) = 1/4 = 0.25 = 25% increase

questions.text: The fifth harmonic of a closed organ pipe is found to be in unison with the first harmonic of an open pipe. The ratio of lengths of closed pipe to that of the open pipe is 5/x. The value of x is ____.

For open pipe, the first harmonic frequency is:
f_1_open = v/(2L_open)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A point source is kept at the center of a spherically enclosed detector. If the volume of the detector increased by 8 times, the intensity will
questions.sol_text:
V → 8V ⇒ R → 2R
⇒ A → 4A
⇒ I → I_0/4

Explanation:
For a spherical detector with a point source at the center:
- Volume V = (4/3)πR^3
- If V → 8V, then (4/3)πR^3 → 8(4/3)πR^3
- This gives R^3 → 8R^3, so R → 2R

The surface area of the sphere is A = 4πR^2
- If R → 2R, then A → 4π(2R)^2 = 4π(4R^2) = 4(4πR^2) = 4A

Intensity is defined as power per unit area:
- I = P/A
- The power P from the point source remains constant
- Initial intensity: I_0 = P/A_0
- Final intensity: I = P/(4A_0) = I_0/4

Therefore, the intensity decreases by a factor of 4, which means it decreases by 4 times (or decreases to 1/4 of original).

questions.text: Two loudspeakers (L1 and L2) are placed with a separation of 10 m, as shown in figure. Both speakers are fed with an audio input signal of same frequency with constant volume. A voice recorder, initially at point A, at equidistance to both loud speakers, is moved by 25 m along the line AB while monitoring the audio signal. The measured signal was found to undergo 10 cycles of minima and maxima during the movement. The frequency of the input signal is ____ Hz. (Speed of sound in air is 324 m/s and sqrt(5) = 2.23)
questions.sol_text:
From the geometry of the setup:

L1 is 10 m away horizontally from the line AB.
Point A is at equidistance from both speakers, located 40 m from L1 horizontally.
B is 25 m above A.

Distance from L1 to point B:
L1B = sqrt(20^2 + 40^2) = sqrt(400 + 1600) = sqrt(2000) = 20*sqrt(5) = 44.6 m

Distance from L2 to point B:
L2B = sqrt(40^2 + 30^2) = sqrt(1600 + 900) = sqrt(2500) = 50 m

Path difference at point B:
Δx = L2B - L1B = 50 - 44.6 = 5.4 m

Path difference at point A (equidistant from both speakers):
Δx = 0 m

Total change in path difference as the recorder moves from A to B:
Δx = 5.4 m

The signal undergoes 10 cycles of minima and maxima during this movement.
10 cycles means the path difference changes by:
Δx = 10 * λ

5.4 = 10 * λ
λ = 0.54 m

Using the wave equation:
v = f * λ
324 = f * 0.54
f = 324/0.54 = 600 Hz
